column1: # What the upstream-drift workflow watches, and the single source of truth for it.
# build/check-upstream.sh reads this; it knows how to query each ecosystem but nothing about which
# components this repository binds. Adding a native SDK means adding a row here.
# Columns are single-tab-separated.
#   group    reporting group - one GitHub issue per group, titled with this text. These mirror the
#            release tracks in build/tracks.tsv on purpose: a drift report then lands on the same
#            axis as the release that fixes it.
#   label    how the component is named inside the issue
#   kind     cocoapods | maven | github-release | github-tag
#   pin      the MSBuild property in Directory.Build.props holding the pinned version
#   locator  kind-specific: pod name, groupId:artifactId[:packaging][@repo], or owner/repo[:strip]
#   confirm  download URL template with {version}, or "-" to follow the vendor's own pointer
#            (for CocoaPods, the podspec's source - the same URL build/fetch-*.sh resolves)
# group
RTC
# Voice checks AgoraRtcEngine_macOS too, not AgoraAudio_macOS: there is no standalone voice-only
# macOS SDK. AgoraAudio_macOS is a dead 3.7.x line, so the Voice package binds the audio surface of
# the same archive the Video package uses - see build/fetch-voice.sh. Pointing this row at the dead
# pod made it read as permanently up to date while comparing a 4.6.2 pin against 3.7.2.
RTC
# RTM 2.x has no macOS pod. Its versions are the tags on AgoraIO/AgoraRtm_Apple - the repository
# whose Package.swift build/fetch-signaling.sh already treats as the source of truth - and the
# artifacts are per-module zips behind download.agora.io/rtm2, so the confirmation is spelled out
# rather than derived. AgoraRtmKit is the module that must exist for the fetch to work at all.
Signaling
